'''Karl Willard Giberson''' (born May 13, 1957) is a Canadian physicist, scholar, and author, specializing in the [[Creationism|creation]]–[[evolution]] debate. He has held a teaching post since 1984, written several books, and been a member of various academic and scientific organizations. He formerly served as vice president of the [[BioLogos Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://biologos.org/blog/karl-giberson-moves-on-to-create-more-time-for-writing |title=Karl Giberson Moves on to Create More Time for Writing &#124; the BioLogos Forum |access-date=2012-07-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150921231014/http://biologos.org/blog/karl-giberson-moves-on-to-create-more-time-for-writing |archive-date=2015-09-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Education==
Giberson holds two [[bachelor's degrees]] (in philosophy and in physics/math) from [[Eastern Nazarene College]], and both a master's degree and a PhD in physics from [[Rice University]].

==Career==
Giberson was a member of the faculty at his alma mater, [[Eastern Nazarene College]], from 1984 to 2011. In that time, he taught courses on physics, astronomy, and science and religion, as well as directing the Honors Scholar Program. His strong support for evolution made him increasingly controversial<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://reformednazarene.wordpress.com/2009/08/11/karl-giberson-promotes-christian-evolution-at-enc/|title = Karl Giberson Promotes "Christian Evolution" at ENC|date = August 11, 2009}}</ref> and played a role in his departure in 2011.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/01/02/2013-was-a-terrible-year-for-evolution.html|title = 2013 Was a Terrible Year for Evolution|newspaper = The Daily Beast|date = January 2, 2014|last1 = Giberson|first1 = Karl W.}}</ref>

Giberson is also a fellow of the [[American Scientific Affiliation]] (ASA). He co-directed the Venice Summer School on Science and Religion,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.enc.edu/news/2008/giberson_yerxa.htm |title=Eastern Nazarene College: News |access-date=2008-12-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080805173808/http://www.enc.edu/news/2008/giberson_yerxa.htm |archive-date=2008-08-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and has lectured on science and religion at [[Oxford University]], the [[Ettore Majorana Foundation and Centre for Scientific Culture]] in Sicily, and various colleges and universities in the United States. In 2006, he was invited to speak at the [[Vatican City|Vatican]] on "America's Ongoing Hostility to Darwinism" and at the [[Harvard Club of New York City]] in 2008.  

In early 2009, Giberson became the Executive Vice President of The [[BioLogos Foundation]], founded by [[Francis Collins]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.biologos.org/about/team/karl-giberson |title=BioLogos.org |access-date=2009-05-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090503221613/http://biologos.org/about/team/karl-giberson/ |archive-date=2009-05-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He served briefly as president before leaving the foundation in 2011 to further pursue his passion for writing.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://biologos.org/about/history |title=Our History: 2006 to Today &#124; BioLogos |accessdate=2015-08-11 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150811080251/http://biologos.org/about/history |archivedate=2015-08-11 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://biologos.org/blog/karl-giberson-moves-on-to-create-more-time-for-writing |title=Karl Giberson Moves on to Create More Time for Writing &#124; the BioLogos Forum |access-date=2012-07-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150921231014/http://biologos.org/blog/karl-giberson-moves-on-to-create-more-time-for-writing |archive-date=2015-09-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2012, Giberson became a faculty member at [[Stonehill College]] in [[Easton, Massachusetts]], where he is a scholar-in-residence in science and religion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stonehill.edu/directory/karl-giberson/|title = Faculty & Staff Directory}}</ref>

In 2013, Giberson was elected to the [[International Society for Science and Religion]] (ISSR).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.issr.org.uk/meet-issr-members/member/?member_id=188|title = Members Login Fellows & Associates}}</ref>

==Published works==
Giberson is a contributing editor to ''Books & Culture'', where he has published many essays on science. He was the founding editor of ''[[Science & Theology News]]'', the leading publication in the field until it ceased publication in 2006, and editor-in-chief of ''[[Science & Spirit]]'' from 2003 to 2006 for the [[John Templeton Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.asa3.org/asa/newsletter/JULAUG01.htm |title=American Scientific Affiliation newsletter, Jul/Aug 2001, Vol. 43 No. 4 |access-date=2007-08-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108201132/http://www.asa3.org/ASA/newsletter/JULAUG01.htm |archive-date=2012-11-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Giberson has published over two hundred articles, reviews, and essays, both technical and popular. In addition to blogging regularly at the [[Huffington Post]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Karl Giberson, Ph.D|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/karl-giberson-phd|publisher=Huffington Post|accessdate=March 25, 2012}}</ref> Giberson has written for ''[[The New York Times]]'',<ref>{{cite news|title=The Evangelical Rejection of Reason|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/10/18/opinion/the-evangelical-rejection-of-reason.html|accessdate=March 25, 2012|newspaper=The New York Times|date=October 17, 2011|author=Karl W. Giberson|author2=Randall J. Stephens}}</ref> [[Salon.com]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Giberson|first=Karl|title=What's wrong with science as religion|url=http://www.salon.com/2008/07/31/religion_science/singleton/|accessdate=March 25, 2012|newspaper=Salon.com|date=July 31, 2008}}</ref> ''[[Discover (magazine)|Discover]]'', ''Perspectives on Science & Faith'', [[CNN.com]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Giberson|first=Karl|title=My Take: Jesus would believe in evolution and so should you|url=http://religion.blogs.cnn.com/2011/04/10/my-take-jesus-would-believe-in-evolution-and-so-should-you/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110411161610/http://religion.blogs.cnn.com/2011/04/10/my-take-jesus-would-believe-in-evolution-and-so-should-you/|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 11, 2011|accessdate=May 19, 2015|newspaper=CNN.com|date=April 10, 2011}}</ref> ''[[Quarterly Review of Biology]]'',<ref>{{cite journal|last=Giberson|first=Karl W.|title=Theology in the Context of Science|journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology|date=December 2010|volume=85|issue=4|pages=485–486|doi=10.1086/656832|jstor=10.1086/656832}}</ref> ''[[Weekly Standard]]'',<ref>{{cite news|last=Giberson|first=Karl|title=Scientific Methods|url=http://www.weeklystandard.com/articles/scientific-methods|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100301041741/http://www.weeklystandard.com/articles/scientific-methods|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 1, 2010|accessdate=March 25, 2012|newspaper=Weekly Standard|date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> ''Christian History'', ''[[Christianity Today]]'', ''Zygon'', ''[[USA Today]]''<ref>{{cite news|last=Giberson|first=Karl W.|title=Atheists, it's time to play well with others|url=https://www.usatoday.com/news/opinion/forum/2010-05-24-column24_ST_N.htm|accessdate=March 25, 2012|newspaper=USA Today|date=May 27, 2010}}</ref> and other publications. He has appeared on many radio shows including [[NPR]]'s ''[[Talk of the Nation]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Evangelical Christians Form Parallel Structure|url=https://www.npr.org/2011/10/20/141557124/evangelical-christians-form-parallel-structure|accessdate=March 25, 2012|newspaper=NPR|date=October 20, 2011}}</ref>

His essay "Say it Ain't So: America's Ongoing Hostility to Religion" appears in the college reader ''What Matters in America''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Goshgarian|first=Gary|title=What Matters in America|year=2010|publisher=Longman Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-205-66922-6}}</ref>

===Books===
*''Worlds Apart: The Unholy War between Religion and Science'', ([[Church of the Nazarene]] and Beacon Hill Press, 1993)<ref>Karl Giberson, ''Worlds Apart: The Unholy War between Religion and Science'', Beacon Hill Press, 1993 {{ISBN|0-8341-1504-2}}</ref> has, despite controversy, been used at various Nazarene and other evangelical colleges to counter [[Christian Fundamentalist]] approaches to "origins".
*''Species of Origins: America’s Search for a Creation Story'' (Rowman & Littlefield Publishers, 2002),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Larson |first=Edward J. |date=2003-11-01 |title=Don't know much Biology |url=https://www.christianitytoday.com/2003/11/dont-know-much-biology/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Christianity Today |language=en-US}}</ref> coauthored with [[Don Yerxa]], garnered recognition as one of the most balanced treatments of the creation–evolution controversy in print. America's leading scholar of [[creationism]], [[Ronald Numbers]], described it as "accessible, accurate, and even-handed."<ref>[http://www.rowmanlittlefield.com/Catalog/Reviews.shtml?command=Search&db=%5EDB/CATALOG.db&eqSKUdata=0742507645 Reviews for Species of Origins] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040920214318/http://www.rowmanlittlefield.com/Catalog/Reviews.shtml?command=Search&db=%5EDB%2FCATALOG.db&eqSKUdata=0742507645 |date=September 20, 2004 }}</ref> It is used as a textbook and has been translated into [[Polish language|Polish]] for an inclusion in a contemporary philosophy series.<ref>[http://wydawnictwomegas.pl/images/uploaded/books/20.jpg Book cover for Polish translation]</ref>
*''The Oracles of Science: Celebrity Scientists Versus God and Religion'' ([[Oxford University Press]], 2006), co-authored with Spanish philosopher [[Mariano Artigas]], examines the purported "abuse of science" in the service of [[secularism]] by six scientists of this generation: [[Carl Sagan]], [[Stephen Jay Gould]], [[E.O. Wilson]], [[Richard Dawkins]], [[Steven Weinberg]], and [[Stephen Hawking]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oracles of Science. Grupo Ciencia, Razón y Fe (CRYF). Universidad de Navarra |url=https://www.unav.edu/web/ciencia-razon-y-fe/oracles-of-science |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Ciencia, Razón y Fe |language=es-ES}}</ref> The book has been translated into Italian, Spanish and Polish.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oup.com/us/catalog/general/subject/ReligionTheology/PhilosophyofReligion/?view=usa&ci=9780195310726 |title=Oxford University Press: Oracles of Science: Karl Giberson |accessdate=2007-07-01 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701140555/http://www.oup.com/us/catalog/general/subject/ReligionTheology/PhilosophyofReligion/?view=usa&ci=9780195310726 |archivedate=2007-07-01 }} "Oracles of Science: Celebrity Scientists versus God and Religion"</ref>
*''Saving Darwin: How to be a Christian and Believe in Evolution'' (HarperOne, 2008),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Review: Saving Darwin {{!}} National Center for Science Education |url=https://ncse.ngo/review-saving-darwin |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=ncse.ngo |language=en}}</ref> was recognized by the Washington Post Book World as "One of the best books of 2008."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Holiday Guide 2008: Gifts - Best Books of 2008 (washingtonpost.com) |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/artsandliving/features/2008/holiday-guide/gifts/best-books-of-2008/index.html |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=www.washingtonpost.com}}</ref>
*''The Language of Science and Faith: Straight Answers to Genuine Questions'' ([[InterVarsity Press]], 2011), coauthored with [[Francis Collins]], aims to show Christians why they need not reject science nor God.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-06-01 |title=A Scientific Analysis of Karl Giberson and Francis Collins’ The Language of Science and Faith |url=https://www.discovery.org/a/16911/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Discovery Institute |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Karl W. Giberson and Francis S. Collins, The Language of Science and Faith |url=https://pneumareview.com/language-science-faith/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=The Pneuma Review}}</ref>
*''Quantum Leap: How John Polkinghorne Found God in Science and Religion'' (Lion UK, 2011),<ref>Dean Nelson and Karl Giberson, ''Quantum Leap: How John Polkinghorne Found God in Science and Religion'', Lion UK, 2011 {{ISBN|0-7459-5401-4}}</ref> coauthored with Dean Nelson, examines the science-and-religion relationship through the lens of the life of physicist and Anglican priest [[John Polkinghorne]].
*''The Anointed: Evangelical Truth in a Secular Age'' (Harvard University Press, 2011) coauthored with [[Randall J. Stephens]], explores how intellectual authority is applied and misapplied in [[Evangelicalism]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=The Anointed - Evangelical Truth in a Secular Age - By Randall J. Stephens and Karl W. Giberson - Book Review |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/01/08/books/review/the-anointed-evangelical-truth-in-a-secular-age-by-randall-j-stephens-and-karl-w-giberson-book-review.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109061919/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/01/08/books/review/the-anointed-evangelical-truth-in-a-secular-age-by-randall-j-stephens-and-karl-w-giberson-book-review.html |archive-date=2012-01-09 |access-date=2026-01-26 |work=New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-08-06 |title=Review of Stephens and Giberson, The Anointed: Evangelical Truth in a Secular Age |url=https://jacksonianamerica.com/2012/08/06/review-of-stephens-and-giberson-the-anointed-evangelical-truth-in-a-secular-age/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Jacksonian America: Society, Personality, and Politics |language=en}}</ref> The authors wrote an op-ed for [[The New York Times]] summarizing some of the issues that the book raises.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Evangelical Rejection of Reason|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/10/18/opinion/the-evangelical-rejection-of-reason.html|accessdate=March 20, 2012|newspaper=The New York Times|date=October 17, 2011|author=Karl Giberson|author2=Randall Stephens}}</ref>
*''The Wonder of the Universe: Hints of God in Our Fine-Tuned World'' (IVP Books, 2012), is an exploration of the religious resonances of our modern understanding of cosmology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Badger |first=Steve |date=2013 |title=The Wonder of the Universe: Hints of God in Our Fine-Tuned World. By Karl W. Giberson. Downers Grove, IL: Intervarsity Press, 2012. Pp. 216. Plates, illustrations, $16.00. |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/rsr.12027_2 |journal=Religious Studies Review |language=en |volume=39 |issue=2 |pages=75–75 |doi=10.1111/rsr.12027_2 |issn=1748-0922|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
*''Seven Glorious Days: A Scientist Retells the Genesis Creation Story'' (Paraclete Press, 2012), explores what the [[Biblical creation story]] would look like if it were written within the framework of modern science.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2012 |title=Seven Glorious Days: A Scientist Retells the Genesis Creation Story by Giberson W Karl, Karl Giberson |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/9781557259288 |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=www.publishersweekly.com}}</ref>
*''Saving the Original Sinner: How Christians Have Used the Bible's First Man to Oppress, Inspire, and Make Sense of the World'' ([[Beacon Press]], 2015), explains how the idea of the Biblical [[Adam]] has evolved throughout the ages and explores the influence that the fall of Adam has had on Western ideas. Giberson contends that the attempts of [[Evangelical Christians]] to preserve a literal interpretation of the [[Biblical creation story]] have contributed to them becoming intellectually isolated in a variety of fields.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saving the Original Sinner, by Karl W. Giberson |url=https://www.christiancentury.org/reviews/2015-07/saving-original-sinner-karl-w-giberson |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=The Christian Century |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Madueme |first=Hans |date=2016-01-15 |title=Adam and Eve: An Evangelical Impasse?—A Review Essay |url=https://christianscholars.com/adam-and-eve-an-evangelical-impasse-a-review-essay/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Christian Scholar’s Review |language=en-US}}</ref>
